preconditions.description: The length of the input string S is between 1 and 10,000 characters.

postconditions.description: The result is a non-empty string representing the longest palindromic substring.
The result is a substring of the input string S.

postconditions.expression: all(S[i] == S[j] for i in range(len(result)) for j in range(i, i + len(result)))
postconditions.description: The result is a palindrome, meaning it reads the same forwards and backwards.

postconditions.expression: len(result) == max(len(substring) for substring in all_substrings(S) if is_palindrome(substring))
postconditions.description: The result is the longest palindromic substring in S.

postconditions.expression: any(result == substring for substring in all_substrings(S) if is_palindrome(substring))
postconditions.description: The result is one of the longest palindromic substrings in S.

postconditions.expression: not any(len(result) < len(substring) and is_palindrome(substring) for substring in all_substrings(S))
postconditions.description: The result is the first longest palindromic substring found in S.
